title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is an unnumbered inserted sheet (archive p. 661) between Grothendieck's pp. 633 and 634 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The setting is a profinite group 𝔊 with a sign character χ_G, whose kernel is 𝔊^+ (for example 𝔊^+ = SL(2,Ẑ) or one of its quotients or subgroups). It carries:
- distinguished elements ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2);
- a procyclic 'cusp' subgroup L_0 generated by ξ_0;
- a subgroup 𝔊^♮ (the decoration written as a superscript, rendered ♮ here);
- a 'Teichmüller-type' group G_{ρ,σ}. Its elements are images of pairs (f, u), where f ∈ 𝔊 and u = (u, μ, ε_2, ε_3) lies in a group Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔊^+) × Ẑ* × μ_2 × μ_2. Here u is an automorphism, μ a cyclotomic-type parameter and ε_2, ε_3 signs, subject to strict normalisation conditions on ρ, σ and ξ_0.

There is a bigger group S_0G = Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔊 projecting onto G_{ρ,σ}. The kernel of this projection is identified with L_0 by the canonical map i_{L_0,SG} of (28). The previous page defines the homomorphism (38), G^♮ → Aut(𝔊^+) × Ẑ* × μ × μ, sending u to (int(u)|𝔊^+, χ(u), ε_2(u), ε_3(u)). Its image is described by conditions (39) (conjugacy conditions on u(ρ), u(σ), u(ξ_0) and stability of 𝔊^♮), and its kernel by (40). The Corollary there sets Z_0 = Cent_{𝔊^+}(L_0) and Z_0^♮ = Z_0 ∩ 𝔊^♮.

This page.
1. Map (42): Z_0^♮ → S_0G^♮, f ↦ f^{-1}·u(f), where u(f) = (int f, 1, 1, 1).
   - u(f) lies in Z_{ρ,σ} because f centralises ξ_0 (so the condition on ξ_0 holds with μ = 1) and f ∈ 𝔊^♮ (so the conjugacy conditions on ρ and σ hold).
   - The element f^{-1}u(f) centralises 𝔊 inside the semidirect product: (f^{-1}u) g (u^{-1}f) = f^{-1}(f g f^{-1}) f = g. Hence f^{-1}u(f) = u(f)f^{-1}, and f ↦ f^{-1}u(f) is a homomorphism (the standard 'inner automorphism twisted by its realiser' trick).
2. Restricted to L_0^♮, the map is the canonical identification (28) of L_0 with Ker(S_0G → G). Moreover L_0^♮ is exactly the inverse image of that kernel.
3. This yields an injective homomorphism (43), Z_0^♮/L_0^♮ ↪ G^♮_{ρ,σ}, whose image is the kernel of (38).
4. Hence the canonical four-term exact sequence (44): 1 → L_0^♮ → Z_0^♮ → G^♮_{ρ,σ} → G̃^♮_{ρ,σ} → 1. Here G̃^♮ ⊂ Aut(𝔊^+) × Ẑ* × μ × μ is the set of (u, μ, ε, ε') satisfying (39).

This is the analogue, for these 'cusped' Teichmüller-type groups, of the classical sequence 1 → Z(π) → π → Aut → Out. The centraliser of the cusp replaces π, and the cusp group replaces the centre.

Remark. The proposition measures how much finer the construction of G_{ρ,σ} as a group of 'decorated' pairs is than simply defining it as a group of automorphisms of 𝔊^+ (augmented by the data μ, ε, ε'). The discrepancy is exactly Z_0^♮/L_0^♮, i.e. centraliser of the cusp modulo the cusp.

Purpose. This serves the study of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-like groups attached to subgroups of the profinite modular group, and the action on (2,3)-generated groups with a marked cusp ('loop equations'). The next page continues with the coarser map (45) to Aut(𝔊^+) × μ × μ and with the normaliser of L_0.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The well-definedness of u(f) ∈ Z_{ρ,σ} for f ∈ Z_0^♮ relies on the strict normalisation conditions defining Z_{ρ,σ} on earlier pages (u(ξ_0) = ξ_0^μ exactly, ρ and σ fixed up to the prescribed 𝔊^♮-conjugation). The page uses this implicitly.

Minor notational looseness: Grothendieck writes S_0G^♮ = Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔊^♮ and uses 'iso' for the restriction to L_0. Strictly, this is the identification of L_0^♮ with the kernel of S_0G → G given in (28), assumed to be an isomorphism there.
The remark's last sentence is unfinished or elliptic ('on aurait besoin des μ, ε, ε' par dessus le marché...').

ideas.what: Homomorphism f ↦ f^{-1}·(int f, 1, 1, 1) from the centraliser of the cusp subgroup into the decorated group S_0G, landing in the centraliser of 𝔊
ideas.modern_name: Standard comparison between inner automorphisms and the group realising them (the 'twisted diagonal' in a semidirect product G ⋊ Aut G)
ideas.where_published: Analogous constructions appear in GT literature, e.g. Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps; not as stated here

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → L_0 → Cent(L_0) → G_{ρ,σ} → G̃_{ρ,σ} → 1, comparing the decorated Teichmüller-type group with its image in Aut(𝔊^+) × Ẑ* × μ × μ
ideas.modern_name: Analogue of 1 → Z(π) → π → Aut(π) → Out(π) for groups with a marked cusp / tangential base point (automorphisms of profinite modular-type groups preserving inertia)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas: Ihara, Nakamura (centralisers of inertia and automorphisms of profinite surface groups), Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as known

ideas.what: Remark that the decorated group G_{ρ,σ} is finer than a mere automorphism group of 𝔊^+, the discrepancy being Z_0/L_0
ideas.modern_name: Distinction between a GT-type group and its image in Out/Aut of the profinite modular group; faithfulness questions
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT literature (Drinfeld; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Hatice Boggi–Lochak on Aut of profinite mapping class groups)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly isolates Cent(cusp)/cusp as the obstruction to recovering his decorated Teichmüller-type groups from automorphism groups of 𝔊^+. On the next page he asserts that the coarser map is in fact injective even for 𝔊^+ = SL(2,Ẑ). This is a small but concrete structural statement in the unpublished 'Longue Marche' sequel. It is consistent with, but predates, later results on centralisers of inertia in profinite modular and surface groups (e.g. Nakamura's work on centralisers of inertia).
missed.quote: Cette proposition fait apparaître dans quelle mesure la construction faite ici de G_{ρ,σ} est plus fine que celle [qui consisterait à] le définir simplement comme un groupe d'automorphismes de 𝔊^+
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly relevant to the history of GT-type actions on the profinite modular group. It shows Grothendieck tracking exactly the inertia-centraliser issues that later became central in anabelian work. Little new mathematics, though.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine group-theoretic exact sequence inside Grothendieck's private development of GT-like groups for the modular group. It is mathematically standard, and its interest is mainly historical: an early, explicit handling of the centraliser of a cusp.
transcription_corrections: The superscript decoration rendered '𝔖' on Z_0, L_0, G_{ρ,σ} and S_0G is the same decoration as '♮' on the previous page (Z_0^♮, L_0^♮, G^♮_{ρ,σ}). The group symbol written \widehat{𝔖} is the script group 𝔊 (𝔊^♮, 𝔊^+), not a hatted 𝔖.
In (42) the underset annotations read: f ∈ 𝔊^♮, u(f) ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}, and u(f) ∈ Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G^♮_{ρ,σ}.
In the condition under (44): 'formé des (u, μ, ε, ε′)', not '(u, ρ, ε, ε′)'.
In the remark: 'où on aurait besoin des μ, ε, ε′ par dessus le marché' (μ, not ρ). 'plus fine que celle :' is likely an elided 'que celle [qui consiste à le définir]'.
Page placement: this archive page (661) is an inserted, unnumbered sheet between Grothendieck's pp. 633 and 634, continuing 'L_0^♮ s'identifie à un sous-groupe central de Z_0^♮'.
